history.text: Founded around 1830 by the Chamba Leko leader Nubunga Dozinga, whose people had been driven west from today's Cameroon by Fulani attacks; he chose the fertile plain by the Donga river, defended by the river and hills, as the old Kwararafa fragmented. Donga became a centralized Chamba kingdom.

language.name: Chamba Daka and Chamba Leko
language.note: Chamba Daka is Dakoid (Benue-Congo); Chamba Leko is an Adamawa language. Glottolog's code here is the Dakoid family.

summary.text: The Chamba, who call themselves Sama, live along the Nigeria–Cameroon border in southern Adamawa and in Taraba. Ganye is called the headquarters of the Sama people, and Ganye, Jada and Toungo LGAs are Chamba land; the Chamba also founded the chiefdom of Donga in Taraba, whose ruler is the Gara Donga. Unusually, the Chamba speak two unrelated languages: Chamba Daka (Dakoid, the larger) and Chamba Leko (Adamawa).
